title: Diwali Gifting Gets Pricier: Pistachio, Almond Prices Surge Ahead of Festival
excerpt: Pistachio prices are up 30–40% and almonds 10–20% as the US-Iran conflict disrupts Iranian supplies, freight rates climb, and a weak rupee inflates import costs — with traders expecting festive sales to fall 10–15%.
body:
• Pistachios are the worst hit: prices are up 30–40% year-on-year — Iranian in-shell pistachios now wholesale at ₹2,950–3,100 per kg and premium Peshawari grades at ₹3,900–4,000 per kg.
  • Almonds rose 10–20%: California kernels trade around ₹1,000–1,070 per kg in Indian wholesale markets on strong festive demand and a tighter US crop.
  • The causes: the US-Iran war disrupting Iranian shipments and freight routes, a sharp rise in container freight rates, a nearly 50% decline in US pistachio yields, and the rupee near record lows at ₹96.31 per dollar.
  • What it means for you: budget 15–30% more for dry-fruit gift boxes this Diwali; whole cashews at ₹900–1,000 per kg are the cheaper alternative, and traders expect festive dry-fruit sales to drop 10–15%.

Opening lead

This Diwali, the familiar dry-fruit gift box is set to cost noticeably more. Pistachio prices have surged 30–40 percent over last year and almonds 10–20 percent, as the US-Iran conflict chokes Iranian supplies, container freight rates climb, and a weak rupee inflates every imported kilogram, The Hindu BusinessLine reported.

Context & Background

India imports the bulk of its pistachios from Iran and the United States, and its almonds overwhelmingly from California. The West Asia conflict has disrupted Iranian shipping routes and the Afghan trade corridor; availability of Iranian pistachios and dates has dropped by around 30 percent, according to Rahul Kamath, vice president of the Nuts & Dry Fruits Council of India. India's pistachio market alone is estimated at ₹5,000 crore, and the country accounts for 20–25 percent of global date consumption.

The supply shock has been compounded on every front: a nearly 50 percent decline in US pistachio crop yields, lower Californian almond output, higher container freight rates, and the rupee sliding to ₹96.31 per dollar — near its record weak — which raises the landed cost of every consignment.

Impact & Analysis

The numbers at wholesale tell the story. Iranian pistachios have risen by about ₹100 per kg in recent days to ₹2,950–3,100 per kg, while higher-end Peshawari grades have climbed to roughly ₹3,900–4,000 per kg, according to commodity tracker CMB News. Roasted pistachio kernels are quoted near ₹1,650–1,700 per kg. California almond kernels in Indian wholesale markets are up ₹20–25 per kg to about ₹1,000–1,070 per kg on festive buying and reduced selling. Pumpkin seeds, pecans, and dates have recorded increases of 5–10 percent.

The price surge is already reshaping buying. Raju Bhatia, Ambassador for India at the International Nuts and Dry Fruits Council, told BusinessLine that traders expect sales to decline 10–15 percent this season on higher international prices and lower crop yields. Consumers are shifting toward cheaper options: retail prices of whole cashews are hovering around ₹900–1,000 per kg, making them the value pick of the festive shelf. The inflation extends beyond the gift box — festive sweets are costlier too, with milk prices up and sugar, dry fruits, and other ingredients all adding to the bill.

Diaspora Angle

NRIs sending Diwali hampers to family in India will feel the same inflation, whether they wire money home for festive shopping or ship gift boxes abroad. One small consolation for those in the United States: almonds are cheaper at the Californian origin than in Indian retail, so gift boxes assembled stateside may stretch further this year.

What's Next

Commodity trackers expect a firmer short-term price bias, especially for premium in-shell pistachios and kernels, with festive demand running strong from August through December. Relief depends on Iranian shipping lanes stabilizing, the rupee finding a floor, and next season's US and Iranian crops — none of which will arrive before Diwali.
